messages.content: You are a friendly cooking assistant with web search and unit conversion tools.
Hi! I'm hosting Maria and Tom on Saturday and want to make proper garlic bread. I have a sourdough loaf, butter, a whole head of garlic, parsley and some parmesan. Do I need anything else?

content.text: The user has most ingredients. Classic garlic butter needs salt and maybe olive oil. Let me check a reliable recipe for oven temperature and timing before answering.
Great base already! Let me quickly check a well-tested recipe for timings.

arguments.query: best garlic bread recipe sourdough butter parmesan

messages.name: web_search
messages.content:
1. Serious Eats – The Best Garlic Bread: roast garlic, mix with softened butter, olive oil, parmesan and parsley; bake at 425°F for 10 minutes then broil 1–2 minutes.

2. BBC Good Food – Sourdough garlic bread: 100g butter, 3 garlic cloves, pinch of sea salt, bake 200°C for 12 minutes wrapped in foil.

3. NYT Cooking – Garlic bread with mozzarella.

content.text: The user is probably in Europe given 'parmesan' spelling doesn't tell much, but BBC uses Celsius. Convert 425°F so both are shown.

You only need two extras: **flaky sea salt** and a splash of **olive oil**.

1. Soften 100 g butter and mash in 4 grated garlic cloves, 2 tbsp chopped parsley, 30 g grated parmesan, a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp olive oil.
2. Slice the sourdough loaf almost all the way through and spread the garlic butter between slices.
3. Wrap in foil and bake at 220 °C (425 °F) for 10 minutes, then open the foil and broil for 2 minutes.

Maria and Tom will love it.

messages.content: Tom is lactose intolerant. What can replace the butter?

content.text: Lactose intolerance – ghee is nearly lactose free, or use olive oil entirely, or a vegan butter. Parmesan is naturally very low in lactose, so it can usually stay.

Swap the butter for **extra virgin olive oil** (use about 80 ml) or **ghee**, which is almost lactose-free. Aged parmesan contains very little lactose, so most people tolerate it. If you want to be extra safe, use nutritional yeast instead of the cheese.
